summary: In San Jose, upgrading or replacing the main electrical service panel needs an electrical permit; like-for-like replacements up to 400 amps can be permitted online.
default_explanation: An electrical permit is required to upgrade the main electrical service panel of a home. San Jose's exemption covers only replacing a branch-circuit breaker of the required capacity in the same location in a one- or two-family home, and the city says to get a permit to replace a main disconnect.
fee_note: San Jose's FY 2025-26 fee schedule bills electrical inspection at a minimum of $315 per hour, with a 40-minute minimum for a service change on one meter up to 600 amps, in addition to the permit issuance fee.

notes.text: The online permit at SJPermits.org covers a service change up to 400 amps only for a like-for-like replacement in the same location with no changes to exterior finishes. Other panel work needs the city's regular permit process.
When service equipment serving a home is replaced, a Type 1 or Type 2 surge-protection device must be installed.
Fees: electrical inspection is a minimum of $315 per hour with a 40-minute minimum for a service change up to 600 amps, plus a permit issuance fee.

Online permits can be pulled only by the property owner or a qualified contractor. The city recommends that a licensed contractor pull the permit; an owner-builder must also submit the Owner Acknowledgement and Information Verification Form, show ID at issuance, and be the owner of record.
San Jose adopted the 2025 California Electrical Code; the 2025 codes apply to permit applications made on or after January 1, 2026.

research_notes: Access: every live sanjoseca.gov URL tried, robots.txt included, returned HTTP 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai) to curl and to WebFetch. City pages were read from raw Internet Archive captures (id_ mode, fetched with curl, tags stripped with python3, the fee schedule PDF read with pdftotext). source_url is the capture URL; the official sanjoseca.gov URL is the part after the timestamp. The captured robots.txt (https://web.archive.org/web/20260501010517/https://www.sanjoseca.gov/robots.txt) disallows only /scripts, /admin and *.asmx for all agents. The city's E-Government Policy (sanjoseca.gov/home/showdocument?id=17869, capture 20260904222013) has no rule against copying or automated access. Internet Archive terms say access 'is granted for scholarship and research purposes only'. Re-check each city quote on the live page before marking a rule verified. Quote format: list items and paragraph breaks are joined with single spaces and bullet characters are left out; ' ... ' marks omitted text; the words are verbatim. sjpermits.org robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /', so the SJPermits portal was not fetched; online-permit availability comes from the city's Online Building Permits page. Municode (host of the San Jose Municipal Code) was not fetched. Its archived terms (https://web.archive.org/web/20190411032708/https://www.municode.com/terms-of-use/) say: 'You may not copy, modify, reproduce, republish, distribute, display, or transmit for commercial, non-profit or public purposes all or any portion of this Website, except to the extent permitted by these Terms and Conditions of Use.' The current terms page could not be loaded. SJMC text: quotes marked 'Ord. No. 31256' come from the council-agenda redline of that ordinance (draft dated 10/16/2025, Council Agenda 10/28/2025 Item 8.2(a), file 25-1131), downloaded through the Legistar Web API (webapi.legistar.com); sanjose.granicus.com robots.txt has 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'. Each such quote is the enacted wording: struck-through text removed and underlined additions kept, checked against the rendered PDF page. Legistar matter 25-1187 (Final Adoption of Ordinances, dated 2025-10-30) lists 'Ordinance No. 31256' as passed for publication on 10/28/2025; the signed ordinance and the final vote were not retrieved. Code edition: San Jose adopted the 2025 California codes (not 2022) for permit applications made on or after January 1, 2026. SJMC 24.09.110(A)(6) does not adopt CRC Chapter 1, Division II, so CRC §R105.2 does not apply in San Jose; the city's exemption lists are SJMC 24.02.120 to 24.02.150. Section numbering: the When Is a Building Permit Required? page (updated 06/12/2025) cites 'Section 24.02.110' for the exempt list, but Ord. No. 31256 amends the exemption lists as 24.02.120 (building), 24.02.130 (plumbing), 24.02.140 (mechanical) and 24.02.150 (electrical). Fees: the fee schedule capture is the FY 2025-26 schedule ('Effective August 11, 2025', document 26047 version 637922894017900000, captured 2025-12-07). The Building Permit Fees page captured 2026-08-01 still says the schedule shows fees in effect as of August 11, 2025, but links a newer upload (version 639180865996470000) with no capture, so the current PDF could not be compared. A draft FY 2026-27 fee resolution (Council Agenda 06-09-2026 Item 3.4(b), Legistar file 26-683) sets different amounts ('Water Heater Replacement – Permit Center 0.25 x # of units $52'); its adoption was not confirmed, so it is not cited. Redline detail: in SJMC 24.02.150 item 6, Ord. No. 31256 adds 'branch circuit' and 'in one- and two-family dwellings' and strikes 'except service equipment'. Both the old and new wording leave the service panel outside the exemption. The 400-amp online condition limits the online path, not whether a permit is needed, so it is a note rather than an outcome. docs_required is empty because the captured page lists no required documents for the online path.
